one_line: Hoysala emperor Veera Ballala II and his queen Umadevi, patrons of rich temple and Jain institutions in 12th–13th century Dorasamudra-Halebidu and Shravanabelagola.

appearance.age_look: Ballala appears mid-40s, broad-shouldered and athletic; Umadevi appears mid-30s, graceful and poised with a firm, confident stance.
appearance.face: Both have warm medium-brown complexions; Ballala has a square jaw, straight nose, neatly trimmed moustache and small goatee with sharp determined eyes and a calm, commanding default expression; Umadevi has an oval face, expressive large eyes, straight nose, gently arched brows, and a composed, slightly serious default expression with a hint of kindness.
appearance.hair: Ballala’s hair is thick, wavy, black, gathered into a low bun at the back, front smoothed and partly covered by a modest gold Hoysala-style crown-band with a small central leaf motif; Umadevi’s long black hair is center-parted, oiled and smooth, drawn back into a single thick braid reaching mid-back, wrapped at the crown with a slim gold band and adorned at the braid end with a small gold jewel clasp.
appearance.costume: Ballala wears a knee-length, fitted silk tunic in deep maroon with short sleeves, subtle woven floral motifs and a high round collar, over cream cotton trousers that taper to the ankle; a rich dark-green silk angavastra with thin gold border drapes from his left shoulder across the chest and around the waist; he has a wide gold waist-belt with simple geometric relief, armlets on both upper arms, and multiple short gold necklaces, with leather sandals on his feet; Umadevi wears a traditional Hoysala-period sari in muted teal-blue silk with a narrow gold border, wrapped in a practical, slightly narrower drape that covers her torso fully, pleats falling to her ankles and pallu brought over her left shoulder; beneath it she has a fitted short-sleeved blouse in soft cream; she is adorned with a layered but dignified set of gold jewellery—medium-length necklace, small earrings, slim bangles, and a single understated nose stud—plus a fabric girdle over the sari at the waist; both costumes avoid fantasy elements, matching South Indian 12th–13th century royal attire.
appearance.signature: Ballala carries a sheathed, gently curved South Indian sword with a simple bronze hilt at his left hip, while Umadevi holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin cord, symbolizing her administrative authority and engagement with inscriptions and merchant patronage.

ref_desc: Veera Ballala II is a medium-brown, square-jawed king in a maroon tunic, cream trousers, dark-green angavastra, gold crown-band and sword, beside Umadevi, medium-brown, oval-faced queen in teal-blue sari, cream blouse, gold jewels and palm-leaf manuscript, both accented in gold and cream.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Veera Ballala II and Queen Umadevi standing side by side: Veera Ballala II is a broad-shouldered, medium-brown man in his mid-40s with a square jaw, neat moustache and small goatee, thick black hair in a low bun, partly covered by a modest gold crown-band with a central leaf motif. He wears a knee-length fitted silk tunic in deep maroon with short sleeves, subtle woven floral patterns and a high round collar, over cream cotton trousers tapering to the ankles, a rich dark-green silk angavastra with a thin gold border draped from his left shoulder across his chest and around his waist, a wide gold waist-belt, gold armlets and short gold necklaces, and plain leather sandals; at his left hip hangs a sheathed gently curved South Indian sword with a simple bronze hilt. Beside him, Queen Umadevi is a graceful, medium-brown woman in her mid-30s with an oval face, large expressive eyes and composed, slightly serious expression, her long black hair center-parted, smoothed and drawn into a single thick braid reaching mid-back, wrapped at the crown with a slim gold band and finished with a small gold jewel clasp at the braid end. She wears a muted teal-blue silk sari with a narrow gold border, draped to cover her torso modestly, pleats falling to her ankles and the pallu over her left shoulder, over a fitted short-sleeved cream blouse, and a fabric girdle at the waist; her jewellery is dignified gold—medium-length necklace, small earrings, slim bangles and a tiny nose stud—and she holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin cord in one hand. Keep their look historically grounded in 12th–13th century Hoysala South India, emphasize the deep maroon, teal blue, dark green, cream and gold palette, and clearly show face, hair, clothing details, jewellery, sandals, sword and manuscript so the characters can be redrawn consistently from any angle.
